clues.text: Filled with rage at Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, King Nebuchadnezzar ordered it heated seven times hotter than usual.
In Babylon, King Nebuchadnezzar looked into its fire and saw four men walking unbound, the fourth like a son of the gods.
Before Pharaoh, Moses tossed handfuls of its soot into the air, and festering boils broke out across Egypt.
The morning after Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed, Abraham saw smoke rising from the plain like smoke from one.
Moses reminded Israel that the LORD had brought them out of Egypt, which he called an iron one.
Jesus said that at the end of the age, angels will throw the wicked into a fiery one, with weeping and gnashing of teeth.
A proverb says a crucible is for silver and this is for gold, but the LORD tests hearts.
